identity: An Arabic school-history multiple-choice exam bank covering modern Egyptian history (Muhammad Ali, the 1919 revolution, the 1952 revolution, the Dual Control era) and Hashemite/Jordanian history, plus two Sira items. 24 paragraphs, one MCQ item each: a question stem - often containing or ending in a dotted fill-in blank - followed by exactly four answer choices whose a/b/c/d labels and separating punctuation have been stripped. This is doctrine register J (textbook / workbook / worksheet), the sub-type where layout IS content: the page furniture is the sentence.
law: Each item is [stem] || [option 1] || [option 2] || [option 3] || [option 4] || <NL>. In the printed source every option carried a label and a mark (a. b. c. d., or a dash, or a cell/tab break) and every stem ended in a colon or a dotted blank; by LAW 0 (the gold is punctuation-derived - reconstruct the ink, not the meaning) each of those marks is a boundary. This yields 125 segments over 564 real tokens, ~4.5 tokens each, squarely inside the register-J band of 3-10, and it matches J2 (each table cell is a segment) and J5 (labels split from their content). The option lists are also maximally parallel asyndetic lists - four masdars, four proper names, four book titles - which is LAW 3 in its purest form, so the two laws agree rather than compete. Connector rules do almost no work inside the stems: every w- present is phrase-level (wa-Filastin, wa-taAwiduhum, wa-ilgha, wa-khassatan, wa-hall, wal-istiqlal, wal-muslimin) and takes no cut under the LAW 1 exception; the single w- that opens a fresh finite clause with a new subject is @372 wa-la yamlik ahad, inside the quoted King Hussein passage, and that one does cut.
reasoning: CALIBRATION FIRST (LAW 6). The opening 200 tokens are not prose at all - they are stem+choices rows. Once I saw that para 3's tail is Cromer / Wingate / Milner / Lee Stack (four British officials in Egypt) and para 2's tail is Amman / Irbid / Salt / Karak (four Jordanian cities), the item template was fixed, and it is confirmed six independent times: the identical Hashemite block al-Husayn b. Talal | Abdallah I | Abdallah II | Talal b. Abdallah closes paras 17, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 with identical token spans. All 24 paragraphs resolve to a stem plus exactly four choices with no residue. That regularity, not my sense of the meaning, is the evidence. || SITE 1, the SEG/d artifact @113-114 (para 6). This is the load-bearing discovery of the document. Para 6 reads ...askariyya wa ijtimaAiyya SEG d iqtisad iyya wa askariyya. The bare 'd' is the surviving fourth option label (dal = option 4) and 'SEG' is a leaked marker token. Their presence proves option labels existed in the source and were stripped everywhere else, which is the direct warrant for cutting between all options in all 24 items. I cut @112 (end of option 3) as hi, and @113 and @114 as lo each: by A1/A2 a label written 'd.' contributes its own dot-boundary, and a leaked SEG marker can only sit at a break. I accept the risk of one false cut here because a miss costs ~5x a false cut (LAW 0) and I am under-cutting 4.8:1. || SITE 2, para 1 stem end, @11 vs @12. The tail is saAd milner wingate eden macdonald - five tokens, which cannot make four pairs, so the pair reading (mufawadat saAd-milner as a single option) fails on arithmetic. The single-name reading works exactly: the stem ends '...known as the negotiations of Saad ___' @12 saAd, then four British counterparts milner / wingate / eden / macdonald - the same option pool as para 3, where wingate and milner are themselves single-token options. Historically the answer is MacDonald (the Sept-Oct 1924 talks whose failure preceded Lee Stack's assassination), which is only available under this parse. Cut @12 med. I deliberately did NOT also hedge @11: I put the pair reading near 0.3, below the ~0.43 break-even at which adding a boundary improves F1. || SITE 3, para 3 mid-stem blank @34. 'rafada al-sir ___ al-mandub al-sami li-misr' is ungrammatical without a blank after al-sir, so the source carried a dotted line there. J4 (a blank in a fill-in exercise is a boundary) says cut. This is the only mid-stem blank in the document; every other item's blank sits at the stem's end, where I am cutting anyway. The J4 precedent is n=1, so lo. || SITE 4, para 16, the only real prose here. The King Hussein quotation on Jerusalem runs 28 tokens if left whole - far outside every band in my register table. Two cuts. (a) @371 Aanhu: 'wa-la yamlik ahadun...' has its own finite verb AND a new subject (ahad), which is LAW 1 at full strength; the 'mundhu Aahd al-khalifa Umar...' that precedes it is a trailing adjunct and correctly takes no cut (LAW 4). (b) @384 Aanha: 'min aqwal al-malik ___' is a source attribution following a quotation, which J3 makes its own segment (cf. sahih al-bukhari, ibn hibban). So: quote || wa-la-yamlik clause || min aqwal al-malik || four names. || SITE 5, para 24 @583. The tail is tarikh misr / shakhsiyyat misr / nahr misr al-thaqafi / al-thaqafa al-misriyya al-qadima. Grouping 2/2/3/3 gives a coherent fourth title (Ancient Egyptian Culture); the alternative 2/2/2/4 leaves 'al-thaqafi' dangling at the head of option 4, which is worse. Para 18 already shows a 3/3/2/2 item, so uneven option lengths are normal here. Cut @583 lo. || WHAT I REFUSED TO CUT, and why. (1) Era markers m/h mid-stem (@208, @224, @344, @410, @445, @452). A2 makes abbreviation dots boundaries, but that precedent is about Latin initials and URL dots; Arabic AD/AH markers in these textbooks carry no period, and these sites sit mid-clause inside a stem with no analogue anywhere in the option structure. Not a coin flip - skipped. (2) @445 wa-ilgha in para 19: 'sudur dustur... wa-ilgha al-qanun...' are two coordinated masdars sharing the single predicate 'min al-injazat'. No new argument, so the LAW 1 exception holds; likewise @171 wa-Filastin, @178 wa-taAwiduhum, @505 wa-khassatan, @530 wa-hall. (3) @208/@209 mathlama: a trailing comparative clause belongs to the clause before it (LAW 4), so para 10's 16-token stem stays whole despite being long for register J. (4) @298/@299 bi-riAasat in para 13: trailing PP inside option b, same rule. (5) @115 iqtisad, where the source word iqtisadiyya is split across two tokens - almost certainly a line-wrap artifact rather than a mark; I put it near 0.3 and left it. || SELF-CHECK AGAINST MY BASE RATE. 125 boundaries, ~4.5 tokens per segment. My batch-1 instinct would have produced roughly 24 segments here - one per paragraph - which is precisely the failure mode that cost me 231 misses. The density I have chosen is the one the register table demands, and the six identical Hashemite option blocks make it verifiable rather than a guess.
